argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow defense of the locked certification decision. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 points and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports launch readiness in the aggregate. Public governance guidance also supports documenting limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing monitoring. But the same admissible record shows the energy outage response segment misses target, that segment is named in two utility pilot commitments, legal review on disclosure is still open, and policy treats named-use-case weaknesses as material unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The supportable position is therefore not clean policy compliance; it is that certification can be defended only as a caveated decision that does not claim the disclosure issue was resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the policy conclusion. At most, avoiding unnecessary escalation is justified because the locked decision can be described accurately and narrowly from the existing record, without overstating that the materiality issue was resolved.
claims_about_policy: The admissible evidence does not satisfy the full policy predicate for treating this as clean compliance. Under the stated policy text, a weakness affecting a named launch use case is material, and product labeling a segment as non-core does not resolve that when customer commitments and open legal review exist. Public model-card and AI-risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not substitute for the internal requirement to disclose, resolve, or obtain approved risk acceptance for a material named-use-case limitation. The most defensible policy interpretation is that the certification decision should be assessed as caveated rather than fully compliant.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows the energy outage response gap was remediated before certification.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for this specific named-use-case limitation.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was completed before launch.
The open legal review and the named utility pilot commitments materially weaken any claim of clean compliance.
